Subject: Pilot ask — quant/batching/cache guidance + pricing options

Hey Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at FastShip is excited about the Optimize toolkit. Before we lock a pilot I need a clearer picture of:

- Recommended quantization for our production footprint (we run mostly A100s, typical seq len ~512, target p50 latency <120ms).
- Typical batching settings you recommend for 200–500 concurrent sessions and mixed short/long requests.
- What a three-month pilot would cost (ballpark credits + any pilot discount) and how that changes with a 6-month commit.
- Any quick wins we should enable from day one (cache policy, KV retention, model variant suggestions).

We expect ~5M generated tokens / month initially (chat + assistant completions). Security: data residency must remain in US-only regions.

Can you loop in whoever owns quantization recommendations and commercial packaging so we can align to procurement? Looking for a one-page MAP + a short runbook for the pilot.

Thanks,

Simon — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (applied ML / quantization) and Dylan (economics / pilot packaging). High-level answers and next steps below; attaching a short pricing summary for the pilot. (Attachment: proposed-pricing-summary.pdf)

Quick anchor (ballpark):
- 3-month pilot (no reserved capacity): $18k–25k in credits / month depending on model variant and caching aggressiveness. We typically offer a 15% pilot discount for first-time pilots.
- 6-month commit (reserved capacity): available — pricing moves to committed credits with up to 25% discount and eligibility for Dedicated burst slots.

Options we recommend for FastShip given your target latency and token profile:
1) Cache-first pilot (recommended start)
   - Enable prefix KV caching for common system prompts and repeated assistant context. Expect 20–40% token-savings on chat-heavy flows.
   - Keep batching conservative (batch size cap 16–32 for p50 <120ms) with aggressive async batching for throughput spikes.
2) Batch-optimized path (higher throughput)
   - Increase batch size (up to 64) and use a higher latency SLO for background/async tasks to get 2–3x throughput improvements.
3) Quantization recommendation (see Karthik's note below for details)
   - Try 8-bit (FP16->INT8) first; if quality is acceptable run a narrow eval for q4 variants.

Deliverables we’ll produce for the pilot:
- One-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones, expected token burn, and rollback conditions.
- Short ops runbook: config for cache TTL, batching knobs, observability dashboards.
- Quantization eval sheet with sample regressions and recommended fallbacks.

Next steps: Karthik can share expected quality vs savings tradeoffs; Dylan will follow up with a concrete pricing worksheet and DocuSign link for a pilot SOW. Happy to set a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow if that helps.

—Vanessa

Simon / Vanessa — quick technical note on quantization and batching tradeoffs so procurement has a concrete reference when deciding commit bands. I also attached a brief mapping file with eval results (FS-MAP-quantization.xlsx).

High level:
- Quantization paths:
  * FP16 (baseline) — best quality, higher cost.
  * INT8 / 8-bit quant (FP16->INT8) — modest memory reduction, typically ~1.6–2x cost savings with negligible quality loss on completion tasks. Good first step.
  * 4-bit (q4 variants) — 2.5–3x cost savings vs FP16 in our tests for autoregressive workloads, but expect a non-zero quality delta (we’ve seen ~4–8% downstream metric drop on sensitive instruction-following prompts). Useful if you need max savings and can tolerate narrow regressions; fallback path required.

- Suggested experimental plan for FastShip (seq len ~512):
  1) Week 0–1: baseline runs on FP16 + collect 1000 representative prompts.
  2) Week 1–2: run INT8 conversion + automated eval (compare on top-1/ROUGE/QA metrics depending on your tasks). If metrics within threshold, promote to pilot.
  3) Week 3–4: sample q4 run on a small holdout; surface top failure modes and set guardrail triggers in production.

- Batching guidance:
  * For interactive flows (p50 target <120ms): keep batching small — effective batch cap 16–32 for mixed short/long requests. Use tail-latency-aware queueing and continuous batching.
  * For async processing (background summarization / reranks): batch up to 64–128 to maximize throughput and lower unit cost.

- Caching / KV advice:
  * Prefix caching for system prompts and repeated context windows yields the largest token savings. Tune TTL conservatively (30–90s) for chat sessions where context re-use is common.
  * KV cache retention: for seq len 512, increasing cache retention reduces compute for long sessions considerably — expect 15–30% token-cost reduction for conversations with >3 turns.

Operational notes: include explicit fallback to FP16 for flagged prompt classes. We can script an automated rollback if q4 regression rate exceeds X% on your eval set. The attached spreadsheet has our conservative savings estimates and sample eval artifacts.

Happy to run a quick joint eval over a small representative dataset if you can share a sanitized sample (or run our eval runner in your environment).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Applied ML, Redwood Inference

- 6-month reserved commit: commit to $18,000 / month effective rate ($129,600 total) with a 25% discount versus on-demand list and access to burst capacity windows.
- Technical guardrails: we’ll run INT8 by default; q4 runs only on gated non-critical paths and with automatic FP16 fallback for any flagged regressions.

Next steps:
